data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'nawwala' which means 'to flow'. Nuwaylah refers to a dewdrop or a precious drop. It is mentioned in the Quran as a symbol of blessings from Allah. data.cultural_impact: In certain Islamic cultures, it is a tradition to name newborns after the sweet smell of dew drops or to wish for blessings upon them, likening them to the precious Nuwaylah drops. It is also used as a poetic and metaphorical term to describe something valuable or precious, and can be a name for a beautiful and ornamental thing, place or occasion.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, Nuwaylah symbolizes the blessings and provisions of Allah, which come in small, precious droplets. Just as a dewdrop glistens in the morning sun, our connection to the Divine is also precious and valuable. The name is a reminder to seek and cherish the blessings of Allah, no matter how small or insignificant they might seem. Additionally, it is a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly pursuits, and to focus on the everlasting blessings that come from Allah alone.
